lineup: Yoichi Murata — leader, arranger, composer, trombone
events.factual_description: COTTON CLUB presents Yoichi Murata Big Band on Wednesday, August 26, 2026, with sets at 6:00 PM and 8:30 PM. The venue identifies this as Murata's big band's first COTTON CLUB appearance and announces a 17-piece lineup led by Murata on trombone, composition and arranging. COTTON CLUB describes the band's sound as distinct from a conventional swing big band, emphasizing fusion and funk; the announced rhythm section is Yudai Sato on keyboards, Takashi Yofu on guitar, Kenji Takamizu on bass and Yuichi Togashiki on drums, surrounded by four trumpets, five saxophones and four trombones including Murata.

en.why_it_matters: This earns a place because the arranging and rhythm language are the event. Murata's big band is not trying to recreate a standard swing book: the brass and reeds sit on a fusion/funk engine, with a veteran Japanese session vocabulary shaped by work across Sadao Watanabe, Orquesta de la Luz, JAGATARA and a long career as an arranger. Seventeen players in COTTON CLUB makes the physical scale of that writing part of the attraction, and the first appearance there gives the night a concrete frame beyond a routine club date.
en.trip_verdict: Actively make room for one of the two sets if the Tokyo calendar is still open on August 26, especially if the trip is tracing Japanese fusion, brass writing and groove. It is strong enough to build the evening around without displacing a truly rare master, premiere or one-off elsewhere in the city.

es.why_it_matters: Entra porque aquí el acontecimiento está en los arreglos y en el lenguaje rítmico. La big band de Murata no intenta reconstruir un libro convencional de swing: metales y maderas se montan sobre una máquina de fusión y funk, con una genealogía japonesa de sesión que pasa por Sadao Watanabe, Orquesta de la Luz, JAGATARA y una carrera larguísima como arreglista. Diecisiete músicos dentro de COTTON CLUB hacen que la escala física de esa escritura sea parte del atractivo, y el debut de la banda en esa sala le da un marco concreto más allá de otra fecha de club.
es.trip_verdict: Sí le haría espacio activamente a uno de los dos sets si el 26 de agosto sigue libre en Tokio, sobre todo si el viaje viene siguiendo fusión japonesa, escritura para metales y groove. Da para construir la noche alrededor del concierto sin desplazar a un maestro realmente raro, un estreno o una fecha irrepetible en otra sala.

events.factual_description: Blue Note Tokyo presents Pacific Jazz Orchestra directed by Chris Walden from November 20 through November 22, 2026. The November 20 sets begin at 6:00 PM and 8:30 PM; the November 21 and 22 sets begin at 4:30 PM and 7:30 PM. Blue Note identifies the Tokyo engagement as a 17-piece big-band configuration of the Los Angeles-based ensemble, which was founded as a 40-piece orchestra, with a program spanning jazz standards and original material. Chris Walden is the only named member on the current event page; the remaining personnel are still TBA.

en.why_it_matters: This belongs on the board because a 17-piece modern jazz orchestra inside Blue Note Tokyo is a different live proposition from a routine quartet date. Walden's value is in arrangement and orchestral color: he can move a large ensemble between straight-ahead jazz, pop vocabulary and cinematic writing without treating the big band as a museum object. The current listing is still intentionally modest editorially because the Tokyo personnel beyond Walden have not been announced and the engagement runs for three nights.
en.trip_verdict: Worth knowing about if the November Tokyo calendar has an opening, particularly for a night centered on arranging and large-ensemble sound. I would consider one of the six sets if convenient, but would keep a scarcer master, reunion, premiere or small-room one-off ahead of it.

es.why_it_matters: Vale estar en el tablero porque una orquesta moderna de jazz de 17 músicos dentro de Blue Note Tokyo es una experiencia distinta a otra fecha rutinaria de cuarteto. El valor de Walden está en el arreglo y el color orquestal: puede mover un ensamble grande entre jazz, vocabulario pop y escritura cinematográfica sin tratar la big band como pieza de museo. La nota se mantiene deliberadamente moderada porque el personal de Tokio, aparte de Walden, todavía no está anunciado y la residencia dura tres noches.
es.trip_verdict: Vale saber que existe si queda un hueco en el calendario de Tokio de noviembre, sobre todo para una noche centrada en arreglos y sonido de gran ensamble. Consideraría uno de los seis sets si acomoda, pero mantendría por delante a un maestro más escaso, una reunión, un estreno o una fecha íntima realmente irrepetible.
